Issued at 402 AM EST Fri Nov 13 2026

PATTERN SYNOPSIS/FORECAST:

Ridging over the western US getting pinched between energy getting 
flung out of the Gulf of AK (as well as some energy off SoCal)...and 
broad troughing over the E. US, reinforced by lobes of energy 
swirling westward from Hudson Bay/Quebec into the Upper Great 
Lakes/Midwest...as a 120+kt upper jet slithers through the flow over 
North America. While things are generally drying out over the 
Midwest/Upper MS Valley with subsidence and incoming high 
pressure...there is some warm advection ongoing across 
northern/eastern Ontario and Hudson Bay as some deeper moisture (and 
warmer temps aloft) sneak westward into the Upper Great 
Lakes...leaving the core of the coldest air overhead attm (850mb 
temps around -8C sneaking into the Straits as of 6z). Upstream 
energy trying to fight against this westward motion...and is making 
very slight progress, though slow going, given low-level flow 
through the Canadian Prairies is nearly parallel to the thermal 
gradient, with weak NE flow (less than 20kts at 850mb) over western 
Ontario/eastern Manitoba beneath 1030mb surface high. Thermal 
gradient is denoted at the surface by stationary boundary stretching 
from the Canadian Rockies down into TX/LA and up into the 
Appalachians...as a cold front stretches from S. TX to N. FL and up 
to a low off the New England coast. Surface trough stretching from 
WI to OH to our south...with another surface trough from Hudson Bay 
into eastern Quebec (associated with that warm advection). Primarily 
NE/NNE lake effect rain/snow bands ongoing attm over both NW and NE 
Lower MI (UpNorthLive studios west of TC had about a half inch of 
slop as of 1130pm); some radar returns are pivoting southward into 
Whitefish Bay ahead of PV max spinning just to our northeast. 

PV max will continue to swirl down across the area this morning, 
exiting toward Chicago this afternoon, and will expect the most 
intense snows to taper off toward midday in its wake. Tonight, 
heights begin to rise and temps aloft begin to warm (closer to -5C 
at 850mb) as the core of the coldest air departs southward...though 
expect some of that moisture over Hudson Bay to advect in late in 
the day into Saturday morning on continued NE flow aloft...and think 
there will still be a bit of activity around into Saturday morning. 
Expectation is for increasing subsidence and influence of high 
pressure on the area going into Saturday night, with overall 
improvement in conditions going into Sunday (though think a bit of 
lake effect may try to hold on early). High pressure looks to 
overtake the region Sunday night into Monday as some energy rides 
over the top of the ridge across central Canada...and southern 
stream energy plods across the Lower MS Valley. Currently expect 
troughing to dig out west and rebuild the ridge axis into the MS 
Valley and Midwest...with increasing return flow across the central 
US going toward midweek, suggesting active weather for the middle of 
the country, and at least something of a warming trend into the 
Midwest. 

FORECAST DETAILS...

Rain/snow showers continue today/tonight into Saturday...incoming PV 
max should boost ongoing lake effect showers through the morning 
into midday or so...most likely reaching the M-55 corridor around 
midday or early afternoon. Some areas could turn back to all rain, 
but think snow will remain in the mix. Deeper moisture looks to 
briefly depart behind this...but another wave (and a bit of deeper 
moisture) dropping in toward 0z tonight should help boost activity 
again late afternoon into the evening hours. Does appear we will get 
into some warm advection aloft tonight, which should lower inversion 
heights, and could limit lake effect QPF a bit overnight. Flow looks 
to turn more north, which suggests convergence will again be 
enhanced downwind of GT Bay into the higher terrain south of 
Traverse City toward Cadillac...ultimately taking on more of a NNW 
idea going into Saturday morning. This could open the door for areas 
downwind of GT Bay to become a bit of a pivot point for lake effect 
snow bands as flow shifts...which could result in higher 
QPF/snowfall totals than otherwise expected....though still, setup 
attm does not look quite as favorable for lake effect as the current 
situation, again, given those lower inversion heights. Falling 
inversion heights could also result in a lack of ice nucleation, 
which could be a problem Friday night/Saturday morning for areas 
that hang onto lake effect AND get to or below freezing. 

Otherwise, think lake effect showers will remain in play into 
Saturday and perhaps early Sunday, though the setup will again be 
less favorable than this morning. NNW to NW flow would bring some 
action into the usual snowbelt locations.
